correctness.rationale: The analytic gauge G_beta(u)=beta^(-1/2)e^(u/beta)F_beta(e^(u/beta)) yields exactly K_beta(s)=h sum_{k>=1}e^(skh)/Gamma(2kh), h=1/beta. Since g_s(0)=0 and g_s'(0)=2, Euler–Maclaurin gives the universal -h²/6 covariance defect with uniform derivatives, no h term and O(h^4). Independently evaluated positive series/quadrature at beta=6,12,24 give beta²(K_beta(0)-L(0))=-0.16789768,-0.16697134,-0.16674264, converging to -1/6. Compact covariance bounds yield proper Gaussian analytic field convergence; nondegenerate (G,G') and Rouché give zero-measure convergence. Riemann–Lebesgue establishes vertical mixing. Edelman–Kostlan gives rho=(log L)''(2t)/pi; small-x reciprocal Gamma leads left 1/(2pi t²), and Stirling saddle around 2x=e^t leads right e^t/(4pi). The annular expectation follows by the standard radial GAF count and cancellation of the gauge term. The asymptotics have the stated nonjoint order of limits.

value.rationale: An explicit scaling limit for zeros of a naturally weighted Gaussian entire-function family at a sharp unit-circle logarithmic boundary is a meaningful new regime separate from fixed-parameter large holes and local origin repulsion. The full reciprocal-Gamma Laplace covariance, nontrivial universal beta^-2 defect and opposite intensity tails quantify the boundary layer and may be used in zero-process comparisons. The result is restricted to unconditioned compact logarithmic windows; this limit and exact correction are not mere numerical fits.
